description:
kith-peer/src/lib.rs: PeerDeliveryError (line 679) is a pub enum, but is_permanent_delivery_error() (line 706) is private (fn, not pub fn).

This creates an API asymmetry: callers that receive a PeerDeliveryError from a pub function (e.g. via PeerHttpClient) cannot ask 'is this error permanent?' without re-implementing the logic themselves. The concept of permanence is defined in the private function but is not exposed as part of the public error type.

Specifically, the 4xx-vs-5xx permanence classification (permanent on 4xx except 429, transient on 5xx/timeout/network) is a retry policy that any outbox worker needs. If a caller maintains its own outbox retry loop, it must independently re-derive this classification from the PeerDeliveryError variant, duplicating logic that already exists in the crate.

Additionally, PeerDeliveryError derives #[derive(Debug, Error)] but not PartialEq, making it impossible to write clean unit tests that match on error variants by value.

Fix: add pub fn is_permanent(&self) -> bool to PeerDeliveryError (or impl PeerDeliveryError). Add #[derive(PartialEq)] so tests can use assert_eq! on error variants.
title: kith-peer: PeerDeliveryError is pub but is_permanent_delivery_error is private
